intent.text: I support fam's baseline: one cross-family reviewer, council only for high-stakes irremediable shifts or a deadlock the reviewer names. What the motion still leaves open is the shape of the review, and that is what decides whether the draft gets better. Ask that the motion require the reviewer to return changes the author can apply: missing steps, wrong dependencies, unstated assumptions, and any check that would not catch a bad landing. A note that only says the plan looks sound, or that a blind spot exists, is a grade. The 43% versus 116/116 figure is about landings, so it justifies separating author from checker; it does not by itself measure reviewer versus council. I would also take indep's anti-anchoring condition: the reviewer writes findings from the plan and the checks before reading the author's justifications. Without those two constraints, we have picked the right person and still allowed the wrong product.
